subject: How are constraints handled under the hood in INLA?

messages.author: e7cc390b005447b3
messages.subject: How are constraints handled under the hood in INLA?
parts:
Dear INLA-users,

I am wondering how constraints are handled internally in INLA (NOT how to  specify them in the software), more specifically a sum to zero constraint on the besag model (intrinsic Gaussian markov random field, where you add a constant to the diagonal to make it SPD.  Rank deficiency 1)

It is unclear to me how INLA calculates the log likelihood of this density in the calculations performed (or does INLA do something else?) 

I have  made some observations below:

From the note "Approximate inference for Hierarchical Gaussian Markov Random Fields Models" by Rue and Martino, on p. 8: "Since linear constraints destroy the sparseness of the precision matrix it will not allow for fast computation of the marginal variances."  A formula is used to correct the marignal variances. 

To sample from such a field it seems like conditioning  by Kriging can be used, see Eq 2.30 in Rue's book Gaussian Markov Random Fields

One can also use algorithm 3.1 in the same book to obtain a sample from this distribution. 

There is an expression for the likelihood, see Eq 2.31, but the expression is only valid for x such that Ax=e is true. In my case A=[1,1,1,1], e=0. How to handle this constraint with log likelihood?  

The software seems to be fast with the constraint, so something clever is done  


Thanks, 

Fredrik

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How are constraints handled under the hood in INLA?
parts:
Hi,

this is described on page 37-38 in the GMRF book. we have compute
without them and then correct for them. We just need to add an epsilion
on the diagonal for those model-components that are intrinsic, like

> INLA:::inla.set.f.default()$diagonal
[1] 1.015113099e-05


H
